---
title: Measles wastewater surveillance scenario
format: gfm
params:
  scenario: baseline
execute:
  echo: true
  warning: false
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(epiworldR)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
source("model.R")
set.seed(137)

# Apply the scenario to the default parameters.
scenario <- read_scenario(
  file     = "scenarios.yml",
  name     = params$scenario,
  defaults = read_parameters("data/parameters.csv")
)
p <- scenario$p

# Detection reports the target share of cases, counting hospitalizations,
# outside and during a public health alert.
hospitalization <- rash_hospitalization_rate(
  probability = p$prob_hospitalization,
  mean        = p$rash_period,
  sd          = p$rash_period_sd
)
detection_for <- function(reporting) {
  rash_detection_rate(
    reporting       = reporting,
    hospitalization = hospitalization,
    mean            = p$rash_period,
    sd              = p$rash_period_sd
  )
}
p$detection_rate <- detection_for(p$reporting_fraction)
p$alert_detection_rate <- detection_for(p$alert_reporting_fraction)
day_names <- c("Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat")

# Default to 1,000 replicates on five cores; fewer help while editing.
nsims <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("WASTEWATER_NSIMS", unset = "1000"))
ncores <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("WASTEWATER_CORES", unset = "5"))
stopifnot(nsims > 0, ncores > 0)
out_dir <- file.path("results", scenario$name)

# Sentences that depend on the scenario.
sampling_days <- paste(day_names[p$ww_sampling_days + 1], collapse = " and ")
alert_text <- if (scenario$response == "wastewater") {
  paste(
    "In this scenario, a positive result also starts or extends the alert,",
    "so wastewater can raise detection before the first case is reported.",
    "Wastewater cannot locate the outbreak, so it cannot act on a single",
    "school."
  )
} else {
  paste(
    "In this scenario only reported cases start the alert; the samples are",
    "recorded but nothing acts on them."
  )
}
```

**Scenario `r scenario$name`** (response: `r scenario$response`).
`r scenario$description`

This report is rendered from [report.qmd](../report.qmd) by the Makefile
target **`r scenario$name`**; scenario settings are in
[scenarios.yml](../scenarios.yml), and outputs in
[results/`r scenario$name`](../results/`r scenario$name`). The model is an
exploratory simulation, not a forecast. The devcontainer pins epiworldR to
commit `2f1a5acc7835c44908fab53261d879afc4335e51` and the Census helper
package to `ddd9201f28b9908c033542f6a2445b84619af1c7`.

## Parameters

Defaults come from [data/parameters.csv](../data/parameters.csv), which lists
their sources; the scenario changes these:

```{r}
#| echo: false
defaults <- read_parameters("data/parameters.csv")
changed <- names(defaults)[
  !mapply(identical, scenario$p[names(defaults)], defaults)
]
if (length(changed)) {
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    parameter = changed,
    default   = vapply(defaults[changed], toString, ""),
    scenario  = vapply(scenario$p[changed], toString, "")
  ), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No parameters differ from the defaults.\n")
}
```

## Population and contacts

The model has `r format(p$n, big.mark = ",")` agents, about a tenth of the
2025 Census estimate for Salt Lake County, with its age distribution. Each
agent is in the community layer; students also join one school. Ages 5-9,
10-14 and three fifths of 15-19 attend elementary, middle and high schools.
Students are dealt at random into schools of about `r p$school_size`; each
simulated school represents a real school of the same level, drawn with
probability proportional to its weighted population share, and keeps that
school's MMR coverage. See [data/utah/README.md](../data/utah/README.md) for
sources and limitations.

Contacts start from the household, work, other and school matrices. The
school layer takes the school contacts within each school age group, divided
among its students; the community layer keeps everything else. Averaged over
an age group, a student's community and school contacts add up to the
all-setting total. Within a school, every pair of students meets with the
same daily probability.

```{r}
# County age distribution, rounded to the model's population size.
age_limits <- seq(0, 75, by = 5)
census_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "cc-est2025-syasex-49.csv", package = "multigroup.vaccine"
)
census <- multigroup.vaccine::getCensusData(
  state_fips  = "49",
  county_name = "Salt Lake County",
  year        = 2025,
  age_groups  = age_limits,
  csv_path    = census_path
)
shares <- census$age_pops / sum(census$age_pops)
pop <- floor(shares * p$n)
remaining <- p$n - sum(pop)
if (remaining > 0) {
  extra <- order(shares * p$n - pop, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(remaining)]
  pop[extra] <- pop[extra] + 1
}

# Reweight national setting-specific matrices and make contacts reciprocal.
us_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "nc-est2025-agesex-res.csv", package = "multigroup.vaccine"
)
us <- read.csv(us_path)
us <- us[us$SEX == 0 & us$AGE < 999, ]
us_pop <- tapply(us$POPESTIMATE2025, findInterval(us$AGE, age_limits), sum)
weights <- (pop / sum(pop)) / as.numeric(us_pop / sum(us_pop))
settings <- c("Household", "Work", "Other", "School")
setting_contacts <- list()
for (setting in settings) {
  path <- file.path("data/epistorm", paste0(setting, "-M-by5_75-matrix.csv"))
  matrix_data <- read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE)
  contacts <- as.matrix(matrix_data[, -1])
  contacts <- t(t(contacts) * weights)
  pairs <- contacts * as.numeric(pop)
  setting_contacts[[setting]] <- (pairs + t(pairs)) / 2 / as.numeric(pop)
}
total_contacts <- Reduce(`+`, setting_contacts)

# Weight each school's within-district share by ACS district population.
schools <- read.csv(
  "data/utah/school_district_schoolID_data_Utah_2025.csv"
)
schools <- schools[schools$county == "Salt Lake", ]
acs <- read.csv(
  "data/utah/acs_Utah_2023_school_districts.csv",
  check.names  = FALSE,
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM"
)
district <- unique(schools$schooldistrictlocation)
labels <- ifelse(
  test = district == "SALT LAKE",
  yes  = "Salt Lake City",
  no   = tools::toTitleCase(tolower(district))
)
columns <- paste0(labels, " School District, UT")
district_pop <- vapply(
  X         = columns,
  FUN       = function(col) sum(acs[[col]][acs[[1]] %in% c(5, 10, 15, 16)]),
  FUN.VALUE = numeric(1)
)
school_weight <- district_pop[match(schools$schooldistrictlocation, district)] *
  schools$popfrac

# Ages 5-9, 10-14 and three fifths of 15-19 attend the three school levels.
age_group <- rep(seq_along(pop) - 1L, pop)
level <- rep(NA_integer_, p$n)
level[age_group == 1L] <- 1L
level[age_group == 2L] <- 2L
older <- which(age_group == 3L)
level[older[sample.int(length(older), floor(length(older) * 3 / 5))]] <- 3L

# Deal students into schools of about the target size.
school_assignment <- assign_schools(
  level        = level,
  source_level = schools$level,
  weight       = school_weight,
  size         = p$school_size
)
school_group <- school_assignment$school
school_source <- school_assignment$source

# Move within-age school contacts to the school layer so that, by age group,
# community plus school contacts match the all-setting matrix.
attendance <- as.numeric(tapply(!is.na(school_group), age_group, mean))
contact_split <- split_school_contacts(
  total      = total_contacts,
  school     = setting_contacts$School,
  attendance = attendance
)
school_probability <- school_contact_prob(
  school      = school_group,
  age_group   = age_group,
  per_student = contact_split$per_student
)

# The shedding kernel is normalized to one per prodromal-onset cohort; it
# runs from ww_t_start days before prodrome onset to ww_t_end after.
tau <- -p$ww_t_start:p$ww_t_end
rise <- p$ww_t_peak + p$ww_t_start
log_shedding <- ifelse(
  test = tau <= p$ww_t_peak,
  yes  = p$ww_log10_vpeak * (tau + p$ww_t_start) / rise,
  no   = p$ww_log10_vpeak * (p$ww_t_end - tau) / (p$ww_t_end - p$ww_t_peak)
)
kernel <- 10^log_shedding
kernel <- kernel / sum(kernel)
setup <- list(
  persons            = list(age_group = age_group, school = school_group),
  community          = contact_split$community,
  school_probability = school_probability,
  vaccinated         = integer(),
  kernel             = kernel
)
c(
  students = sum(!is.na(school_group)),
  schools  = length(school_source)
)
```

## Vaccination

Students take their school's MMR coverage. Everyone else follows the adult
immunization assumptions used for the Utah/Arizona border in
multigroup.vaccine: under 1s are unvaccinated, ages 1-4 take the county's
elementary-school coverage, ages 5-24 out of school the high-school coverage,
ages 25-44 the mean of the high-school coverage and `r p$adult_vax_coverage`,
ages 45-69 `r p$adult_vax_coverage`, and agents aged `r p$immune_age` and over
count as vaccinated. Vaccination reduces susceptibility by
`r 100 * p$vax_efficacy`% per contact. Coverage is not effectiveness.

```{r}
# County coverage by school level, weighted like the school draws.
level_coverage <- vapply(
  X         = 1:3,
  FUN       = function(j) {
    keep <- schools$level == j & !is.na(schools$vaxrate) &
      !is.na(school_weight)
    weighted.mean(schools$vaxrate[keep], school_weight[keep])
  },
  FUN.VALUE = numeric(1)
)

# Non-students: average the single-year rule over the ages out of school.
out_of_school <- lapply(seq_along(age_limits), function(g) {
  ages <- age_limits[g] + 0:4
  if (g == 4L) ages <- 18:19
  ages
})
band_coverage <- vapply(
  X         = out_of_school,
  FUN       = function(ages) {
    mean(community_coverage(
      age         = ages,
      elementary  = level_coverage[1],
      high_school = level_coverage[3],
      adult       = p$adult_vax_coverage,
      immune_age  = p$immune_age
    ))
  },
  FUN.VALUE = numeric(1)
)

# Students take their school's coverage, or their level's if it is missing.
vaccine_probability <- band_coverage[age_group + 1L]
students <- !is.na(school_group)
school_rate <- schools$vaxrate[school_source[school_group[students] + 1L]]
level_rate <- level_coverage[level[students]]
vaccine_probability[students] <- ifelse(
  test = is.na(school_rate),
  yes  = level_rate,
  no   = school_rate
)
setup$vaccinated <- which(runif(p$n) < vaccine_probability) - 1L

coverage <- data.frame(
  age_group = paste0(age_limits, c(paste0("-", age_limits[-1] - 1), "+")),
  agents    = pop,
  coverage  = round(tapply(vaccine_probability, age_group, mean), 3)
)
knitr::kable(coverage, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Calibrate transmission

Contacts stay fixed; we calibrate only the per-contact transmission
probability. The target is an average of `r p$R0` secondary infections per
imported case in a fully susceptible (unvaccinated) population with no
response, an
illustrative assumption below published measles estimates. The
next-generation approximation gives the starting value, and simulations with
fixed seeds refine it, so scenarios with the same population and natural
history get the same rate.

```{r}
# Start from the analytic value, then correct it with simulated R0.
p$transmission_rate <- transmission_for_r0(p, total_contacts)
analytic_rate <- p$transmission_rate
cal_setup <- setup
cal_setup$vaccinated <- integer()
cal_p <- p
cal_p$n_seed <- 10
cal_p$ndays <- 60
cal_seeds <- 42L + 1:5
cal_nsims <- 10L
for (iteration in 1:4) {
  secondary <- parallel::mclapply(
    X        = cal_seeds,
    FUN      = function(seed) {
      model <- build_model(
        p     = cal_p,
        setup = cal_setup,
        state = new.env(parent = emptyenv())
      )
      run_multiple(
        m        = model,
        ndays    = cal_p$ndays,
        nsims    = cal_nsims,
        seed     = seed,
        saver    = make_saver("reproductive"),
        nthreads = 1,
        verbose  = FALSE
      )
      r <- run_multiple_get_results(model, nthreads = 1)$reproductive
      sum(r$rt[r$source >= 0 & r$source_exposure_date == 0])
    },
    mc.cores = ncores
  )
  if (!all(vapply(secondary, is.numeric, TRUE))) stop(secondary)
  r0 <- sum(unlist(secondary)) /
    (length(cal_seeds) * cal_nsims * cal_p$n_seed)
  if (!is.finite(r0) || r0 <= 0) stop("Calibration produced no transmission")
  if (iteration < 4) {
    cal_p$transmission_rate <- min(1, cal_p$transmission_rate * p$R0 / r0)
  }
}
p$transmission_rate <- cal_p$transmission_rate
if (p$transmission_rate >= 1 || abs(r0 / p$R0 - 1) > 0.1) {
  stop("Calibration failed: simulated R0 ", round(r0, 2))
}
c(
  analytic_rate     = analytic_rate,
  transmission_rate = p$transmission_rate,
  simulated_r0      = r0
)
```

## Surveillance and response

`r 100 * p$reporting_fraction`% of cases are reported. Each day of rash, a
case is detected with probability `r round(p$detection_rate, 3)` and
isolated, and hospitalized cases (`r 100 * p$prob_hospitalization`% of
infections) are always detected; the detection probability is solved so
that, together, they report `r 100 * p$reporting_fraction`% of cases.
Detected cases are reported `r p$case_report_delay` days later.

Any reported case starts or extends a county-wide public health alert of
`r p$response_days` days (health alerts to clinicians, more testing). During
the alert, the daily detection probability rises to
`r round(p$alert_detection_rate, 3)`, which reports
`r 100 * p$alert_reporting_fraction`% of cases, and a vaccination campaign
runs: each day, every agent not yet vaccinated and not detected as a case
receives an MMR dose with probability `r p$campaign_rate` (about
`r round(100 * (1 - (1 - p$campaign_rate)^p$response_days))`% of them over
one `r p$response_days`-day alert; see [literature.md](../literature.md)).
Doses also go to agents with undetected infections, as in practice, but
protect only susceptible agents, from the next day. A reported student case also
excludes the unvaccinated students of that
school who have not been detected as cases. They return `r p$response_days`
days after the school's last reported case, and a school can be excluded
more than once.

Infected agents shed into wastewater from `r p$ww_t_start` days before
prodrome onset until `r p$ww_t_end` days after it, peaking at rash onset.
Wastewater is sampled on `r sampling_days`, and results arrive
`r p$ww_lab_delay` days after sampling. A sample is positive if it reaches
the limit of detection or, with probability `r p$ww_false_positive`,
falsely. `r alert_text`

## Run the replicates

Each of `r nsims` replicates draws an origin school uniformly at random and
infects `r p$n_seed` of its students. Every scenario uses the same replicate
seeds, population and vaccination, so replicate *i* of two scenarios is
identical until their settings make them diverge; compare scenarios within
replicates. Replicates run in parallel across forked R processes, each with
`run()`, because the R event cannot share threads.

```{r}
replicate_seeds <- 1000L + seq_len(nsims)
school_ids <- seq_along(school_source) - 1L
runs <- parallel::mclapply(
  X        = seq_len(nsims),
  FUN      = function(i) {
    set.seed(replicate_seeds[i])
    seed_school <- school_ids[sample.int(length(school_ids), 1)]
    seeded <- which(school_group == seed_school) - 1L
    seeds <- seeded[sample.int(length(seeded), p$n_seed)]
    state <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    model <- build_model(p, setup, state, scenario$response, seeds = seeds)
    verbose_off(model)
    run(model, ndays = p$ndays, seed = replicate_seeds[i])
    c(
      list(
        replicate   = i,
        seed        = replicate_seeds[i],
        seed_school = seed_school
      ),
      state$runs[[1]]
    )
  },
  mc.cores = ncores
)
failed <- !vapply(runs, is.list, TRUE)
if (any(failed)) stop(runs[[which(failed)[1]]])
```

## Outputs

The report writes three tables, a figure, and a metadata file to
[results/`r scenario$name`](../results/`r scenario$name`);
[results/README.md](../results/README.md)
describes every column. Counts are for the
`r format(p$n, big.mark = ",")`-agent model; multiply by `county_scale` in
`metadata.csv` for county totals.

```{r}
# Summarize each run and keep its daily series and age distribution.
first_day <- function(x) if (any(x, na.rm = TRUE)) which(x)[1] else NA_integer_
replicates <- rbindlist(lapply(runs, function(x) {
  d <- x$daily
  data.table(
    scenario                    = scenario$name,
    response                    = scenario$response,
    replicate                   = x$replicate,
    seed                        = x$seed,
    seed_school                 = x$seed_school,
    infections                  = sum(x$infections_by_age),
    rash_cases                  = sum(d$new_rash),
    detected_cases              = sum(d$new_detected),
    reported_cases              = sum(d$reported),
    first_report_day            = first_day(d$reported > 0),
    admissions                  = sum(d$admissions),
    hospital_days               = sum(d$hospitalized),
    isolation_days              = sum(d$isolated),
    last_infection_day          = max(c(0L, which(d$new_infections > 0))),
    active_at_end               = x$active_at_end,
    samples                     = sum(!is.na(d$ww_positive)),
    positive_samples            = sum(d$ww_positive, na.rm = TRUE),
    false_positive_samples      = sum(d$ww_false, na.rm = TRUE),
    alerts                      = x$alerts,
    first_alert_day             = x$first_alert,
    first_alert_trigger         = x$first_trigger,
    first_true_positive_day     = first_day(d$ww_positive & !d$ww_false) +
      p$ww_lab_delay,
    alert_days                  = sum(d$alert_on),
    exclusion_episodes          = x$episodes,
    first_exclusion_day         = x$first_exclusion,
    excluded_student_days       = sum(d$excluded),
    campaign_doses              = sum(d$doses)
  )
}))
daily <- rbindlist(lapply(runs, function(x) {
  cbind(
    data.table(scenario = scenario$name, replicate = x$replicate),
    x$daily
  )
}))
infections_by_age <- rbindlist(lapply(runs, function(x) {
  data.table(
    scenario   = scenario$name,
    replicate  = x$replicate,
    age_group  = coverage$age_group,
    infections = x$infections_by_age
  )
}))

# Record what produced the results.
metadata <- data.table(
  name  = c(
    "scenario", "response", "description", "n", "county_population",
    "county_scale", "replicates", "schools", "transmission_rate",
    "simulated_r0", "epiworldR_commit", "git_commit", "rendered"
  ),
  value = c(
    scenario$name, scenario$response, scenario$description, p$n,
    sum(census$age_pops), sum(census$age_pops) / p$n, nsims,
    length(school_source), p$transmission_rate, r0,
    packageDescription("epiworldR")$RemoteSha %||% NA_character_,
    system("git rev-parse HEAD", intern = TRUE),
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z")
  )
)
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
fwrite(replicates, file.path(out_dir, "replicates.csv"))
fwrite(daily, file.path(out_dir, "daily.csv.gz"))
fwrite(infections_by_age, file.path(out_dir, "infections_by_age.csv"))
fwrite(metadata, file.path(out_dir, "metadata.csv"))
```

## Results

Outcomes per replicate, including introductions that die out. Outbreak
sizes are skewed, so the table shows quantiles as well as means.

```{r}
#| echo: false
outcomes <- c(
  "infections", "admissions", "hospital_days", "isolation_days",
  "excluded_student_days", "exclusion_episodes", "samples",
  "positive_samples", "false_positive_samples", "alerts", "alert_days",
  "campaign_doses"
)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    outcome = outcomes,
    mean    = vapply(replicates[, ..outcomes], mean, 0),
    median  = vapply(replicates[, ..outcomes], median, 0),
    q90     = vapply(replicates[, ..outcomes], quantile, 0, probs = 0.9),
    max     = vapply(replicates[, ..outcomes], max, 0)
  ),
  digits = 1
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
reported <- replicates[!is.na(first_report_day)]
reported_pct <- round(
  100 * sum(replicates$reported_cases) / sum(replicates$infections)
)
timing <- c(
  report = median(reported$first_report_day),
  alert  = median(reported$first_true_positive_day, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

Across replicates, `r reported_pct`% of infections were reported
(`r 100 * p$reporting_fraction`% outside alerts and
`r 100 * p$alert_reporting_fraction`% during them). Of the replicates,
`r nrow(reported)` had a reported case. In those, the median day of the
first case report was `r timing[["report"]]`, and of the first
true-positive wastewater result `r timing[["alert"]]`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-incidence
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Mean daily new infections, excluded students and campaign doses
#|   across replicates, including those that die out.
incidence <- daily[, .(
  `New infections`    = mean(new_infections),
  `Excluded students` = mean(excluded),
  `Campaign doses`    = mean(doses)
), by = day]
incidence <- melt(incidence, id.vars = "day")
ggplot(incidence, aes(day, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Mean per replicate") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Limitations

School assignments approximate enrollment from district population shares,
and the model holds a sample of schools rather than every school. The
wastewater process assumes the whole modeled population contributes to one
catchment, so an alert cannot be traced to a school. Vaccination reduces each
contact's infection probability rather than fully protecting a share of
vaccinated agents, and adult coverage is assumed. Excluded students keep
their community contacts, and non-student cases trigger no school action.
The reporting fraction comes from one outbreak in southwest Utah and may
differ in Salt Lake County, and the reporting fraction during an alert is
assumed. The campaign rate is derived from two outbreak responses (New
York City and Swansea) rather than from Utah; it reaches every unvaccinated
agent equally, ignores the targeting of exposed people within 72 hours, and
does not let excluded students return once vaccinated. These are modeling
assumptions, not
estimates validated against observed Salt Lake County outbreaks.
